chapter: Working life: spot jobs, day jobs, nightclubs
title: How picnic jobs worked and what tunes they played
summary: At picnics he played from nine to six with breaks, without pianos, doing polkas, foxtrots, one steps and waltzes.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: i don't want to wait in chicago pretty with every big thing that there was to have because he worked for all my all of them i guess everything that was up there in fact they were the first ones went up with the dixie lane band him and tom brown in that place they were the first ones i wanted to ask you about the picnics how'd you play there well you played all day

from nine o'clock in the morning till six o'clock in the evening you played a few tunes and then you stopped and got a drink a sandwich or something and then you went back and you played again and that went on all day like that you played anything you wanted to anything at all anything you felt like playing you was the boss nobody to tell you nothing you might get a request maybe somebody come and ask my walls once in a while
They had no pianos at the picnic, you know.
Well what kind of tunes did you play in general? Would you play polkas at all?
Play polkas, foxtrots, one steps, waltzes, lances, varieties, all that kind of stuff. Ever play any quadrilles? No, I don't think I remember of ever playing any of them.
